draft.title: Characteristics of a trading business
card: A trading business buys finished goods and resells them at a higher price. It does not make the goods itself.
buys goods ready for sale and earns income from selling them, such as a hardware store or a shoe shop.
makes goods from materials, then sells them. A furniture maker that builds tables from timber is an example.
earns income by doing work for clients, not by selling goods. A hair salon or a tutoring business is an example.
draft.remember: A trading business buys finished goods and resells them for more than it paid.

a.q: Which business is a trading business?
opts: Ravi buys phone cases from a supplier and sells them online
Ravi sews phone cases from leather and sells them online
Ravi repairs cracked phone screens for a fee
Ravi teaches classes on how to use a smartphone
a.why: Ravi buys finished phone cases and resells them, which is what a trading business does. The leather business makes its own goods, so it is a manufacturer. The other two earn income from services.
a.clue: Which business buys finished goods and does not make them?

b.q: Mia buys timber and cuts it into garden benches, then sells them at a market stall. Why is Mia's business not a trading business?
opts: It makes the goods it sells instead of buying them finished
It sells goods to customers at a market stall, not in a shop
It sells goods at a higher price than the cost of timber
It earns income from selling goods instead of from services
b.why: A trading business buys finished goods and resells them. Mia turns timber into benches, so she makes the goods and is a manufacturer. Selling goods for a profit does not make a business a trading business, because manufacturers do that too.
b.clue: Look at what Mia buys: is it finished goods or materials?

a.best: Ravi buys phone cases from a supplier and sells them online

b.best: It makes the goods it sells instead of buying them finished
